scope: Current runtime/provider/context implementation and relevant new regression boundaries

findings.title: New optional image work bypasses mandatory text finishing priority
findings.session_relation: Incomplete integration of the new text priority guard with the unchanged image capacity path.
findings.trigger: A text run has reached synthesis/audit and a queued optional generation/edit is evaluated while shared slots are available or about to free.
findings.observed: provider_capacity_available(... mandatory=False) returns False; image_tasks._capacity returns True for the same shared capacity state. Image execution never consults the new stage-priority guard.
findings.impact: New optional image work can acquire shared provider/global capacity ahead of ready mandatory text work. Alongside existing visual critics it can occupy all slots and exhaust the text run's reserved finishing opportunity.
findings.fix: Use one locked shared capacity/admission policy for both text and image authorization, preserving required visual reviews while denying new optional generation/edit ahead of admitted mandatory text work. Include cross-modal scheduling regressions.
findings.caveat: The direct probe verifies actual guard disagreement. It does not claim every scheduling order starves text, that a single image call fills all slots, or that monetary/call caps are bypassed.

findings.title: Preflight accepts input that configured provider context admission necessarily rejects
findings.session_relation: The new exact-byte helper checks the application48K packet ceiling but does not apply configured provider schema/system/output bounds.
findings.trigger: A valid brief contains12,000 background characters,4,000 goal characters and4,000 question characters, with verified configured context32,768 and ordinary synthetic prices.
findings.observed: input_packet_error returns None; the actual intake packet is32,325 bytes (under48K), while HTTPProvider.conservative_bound rejects context_limit after adding wire schema/system/protocol margin and billable output allowance.
findings.impact: A successful-looking funded preflight can admit a run whose intake cannot start; one preflight is consumed and a failed/limited report results without substantive model work. Mandatory finishing contexts can encounter the same configuration mismatch later.
findings.fix: Apply the adapter's no-send conservative payload/context calculation at preflight for configured mandatory roles and credible downstream envelopes, including schemas, instructions, output bound and provider context. Surface a precise blocker before Start.
findings.caveat: Pre-send provider checks correctly prevent an oversized external request; this is admission/liveness and misleading readiness-to-start, not a paid context-overflow send. The synthetic configuration uses valid public data and no key/network access.

findings.title: Moderator pre-send recovery cycles the first two fallback providers
findings.session_relation: Pre-existing unchanged fallback loop remains in a runtime file modified this session; record separately from newly introduced defects.
findings.trigger: OpenAI and Anthropic fail conservative pre-send configuration validation while Google is healthy; declared fallback order is OpenAI, Anthropic, Google.
findings.observed: Three infrastructure claims evaluate OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenAI; the run fails with zero authorized model calls and Google is never attempted.
findings.impact: A declared healthy moderator fallback is skipped even when it fits the remaining infrastructure and paid-call limits. This can prevent a usable stage from executing after provider credential/configuration availability changes.
findings.fix: Persist attempted/unavailable providers per logical role and advance through eligible predeclared fallbacks in order, retaining all original call/infrastructure/refusal guards.
findings.caveat: Ordinary sent failures still have only the original two-call ceiling; this reproduction uses pre-send failures that consume zero model calls. It does not authorize extra paid calls or fallback to evade refusal.
